'''Michael Richard Edward Proctor''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FIMA|FRAS}} (born 19 September 1950)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Proctor, Prof. Michael Richard Edward | id = U151348 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U151348 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is a British physicist, mathematician, and academic. He is Professor of Astrophysical Fluid Dynamics at the [[University of Cambridge]] and, until 2023, served as the [[Provost (education)|Provost]] of [[King's College, Cambridge]] and [[school governor]] at [[Eton College]].<ref name=governors>{{cite web|url=https://www.etoncollege.com/about-us/our-governing-body/|website=etoncollege.com|title=Our Governing Body}}</ref><ref name="bio - Debrett's">{{cite web|title=Michael Richard Edward PROCTOR|url=http://www.debretts.com/people-of-today/profile/21464/Michael-Richard-Edward-PROCTOR|work=People of Today|publisher=[[Debrett's]]|accessdate=2014-05-03|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924040235/http://www.debretts.com/people-of-today/profile/21464/Michael-Richard-Edward-PROCTOR|archivedate=24 September 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="bio - DAMTP Personal website">{{cite web|title=Michael Proctor ScD FRS FIMA|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/mrep/|work=Personal website|publisher=Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics|accessdate=2014-05-03}}</ref><ref>[https://www.sms.csx.cam.ac.uk/media/2904282 Interviewed by Alan Macfarlane 11 September 2018 (video)]</ref>

==Early life and education==
Proctor was born on 19 September 1950 in [[Bournemouth]], [[Dorset]]. The son of a farmer, he grew up in [[Spalding, Lincolnshire]]. He was educated at [[Shrewsbury School]]<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> and won a scholarship to study [[Mathematical Tripos|mathematics]] at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]],<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Michael Richard Edward Proctor: Curriculum Vitae|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/mrep/jobcv.pdf|accessdate=2014-05-03}}</ref> and [[matriculated]] at the college in 1968.<ref name="New Provost-elect of the College" /> He achieved a distinction in [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]] and then graduated in 1972 with a [[Master of Mathematics]] (MMath) degree.<ref name=CV /> From 1972 to 1973, he was a [[Kennedy Scholar]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in the United States.<ref name="CV 21">{{cite web |title=Michael Richard Edward Proctor FRS: Curriculum Vitae |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/mrep/latestcv.pdf |website=Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics |publisher=University of Oxford |access-date=23 February 2023 |date=5 August 2021}}</ref> He then returned to the [[University of Cambridge]] to undertake [[postgraduate research]] supervised by [[Keith Moffatt]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref name=CV /> He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree in July 1975 on non-linear mean field dynamo models.<ref name="CV 21" /><ref name=PhD-469560>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=https://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/permalink/f/t9gok8/44CAM_ALMA21431209110003606|title=Non-linear mean field dynamo models and related topics|first= Richard Edward Proctor|last=Proctor|date=1975|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.469560}}|website=cam.ac.uk|oclc=503075350}}</ref><ref name=CV /> In 1995, he was awarded a [[Doctor of Science]] (ScD) degree, a [[higher doctorate]], by the University of Cambridge.<ref name="CV 21" />

==Career and research==
In 1974, Proctor was elected a [[Fellow]] of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> From 1975 to 1977, he was a postdoctoral researcher and assistant professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="bio - DAMTP">{{cite web|title=Professor Michael Proctor|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/m.r.e.proctor/|work=People|publisher=Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics|accessdate=2014-05-03}}</ref> He returned to the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1977 as an [[lecturer|assistant lecturer]] in the [[Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref name="bio - DAMTP" /> In the same year he was appointed a college lecturer at Trinity College, Cambridge.<ref name=CV /> He served as a [[tutor]] at Trinity from 1979 to 1991, and from 1992 to 1994.<ref name="bio - DAMTP" /> At university level, he was promoted to lecturer in 1982.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" />

He was promoted to [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] in 1994.<ref name="damtp bio">{{cite web |title=Professor Michael Richard Edward Proctor {{!}} Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/person/mrep |website=Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=23 February 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In the same year, he was elected [[Dean (education)#United Kingdom|Dean]] of Trinity College.<ref name="bio - DAMTP" /> In 2000, he was appointed Professor of Astrophysical Fluid dynamics.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> He was elected [[Master (college)|Vice-Master]] of Trinity College in 2006.<ref name=whoswho/><ref name="bio - DAMTP" /> In 2012, he was elected [[Provost (education)|Provost]] of [[King's College, Cambridge]].<ref name="New Provost-elect of the College">{{cite web|title=New Provost-elect of the College|url=http://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/news/2012/new-provost-elect-college.html|work=News|publisher=King's College, Cambridge|accessdate=2014-05-03|year=2012}}</ref> He moved from Trinity to King's to take up the position at the start of the 2013 academic year.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> On 2 May 2017, he was re-elected for a second five-year term as provost from 1 October 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Michael Proctor re-elected |url=https://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/news/2019/professor-michael-proctor-re-elected |website=King's College |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=23 February 2023 |language=en |date=8 May 2017}}</ref>

===Honours and awards===
In 1977, Proctor was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society]] (FRAS).<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> He was awarded a [[Doctor of Science]] (ScD) degree by the University of Cambridge in 1995.<ref name=CV /> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2006,<ref name=whoswho/><ref>{{cite web|title=Awards and prizes|url=https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/univ/annualreport/2006/awards.html|publisher=[[University of Cambridge]]|accessdate=2014-05-03|year=2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Current Fellows|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/|work=Fellowship of the Royal Society|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|accessdate=2014-05-03}}</ref> and as a [[Fellow of the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] (FIMA) in 2007.<ref name="bio - Debrett's"/>
